keyPlatformPillars.details: Maintain essential city services while adhering strictly to state budget caps. Champion municipal property tax relief programs and expanded recreational opportunities for seniors and youth.

keyPlatformPillars.details: Ensure competitive patrol staffing levels, modernize frontline firefighting gear, and complete crucial facility improvements for Clifton's emergency responders.

Licensed Private Investigation & Security Inquiries

notableControversies.title: City Hall Mass Resignation Fallout & Legal Turmoil
notableControversies.details: As Mayor presiding over the council, Grabowski faced intense community and political scrutiny during the abrupt mass departures of City Manager Nick Villano, City Attorney Matthew Priore, Personnel Director Douglas Johnson, and CFO Joseph Kunz. Multiple former department heads subsequently filed tort notices and civil lawsuits against the city, exposing deep friction inside City Hall.
notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: City Council operated with interim leadership and appointed special outside counsel; Grabowski publicly called for ending personal attacks and focusing on governance and decorum.

notableControversies.title: Outside Landscaping & Dual Commercial Holdings Monitoring

notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: Disclosed on annual State FDS; subject to mandatory Local Government Ethics Law recusal requirements.

investigativeDossier.conflictOfInterestWatch: Under N.J.S.A. 40A:9-22.1, may not vote or participate in any municipal contract, vendor award, or code enforcement dispute affecting private landscaping, studio, or consulting clients.

notableControversies.title: Dais Feud & 'Musical Chairs' Stand-off with Rosemary Pino

notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: Council meetings experienced prolonged procedural delays; became a focal point of 2026 campaign debates on dais civility.

councilCandidates.name: Avraham Shaya Eisenman
councilCandidates.experience: Clifton small business proprietor, local commercial property manager, active community volunteer and civic participant.
councilCandidates.tagline: A proposed 2-year municipal tax freeze, retail support on Clifton and Van Houten corridors, and citizen participation at council meetings.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Two-Year Municipal Property Tax Freeze
keyPlatformPillars.details: Enact an immediate two-year moratorium on municipal tax hikes. Reallocate surplus reserves and audit vendor billing to stabilize tax bills for hard-pressed homeowners.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Revitalizing Local Retail & Dining Corridors
keyPlatformPillars.details: Work with merchant groups along Van Houten Ave, Clifton Ave, and Lakeview to implement pedestrian-friendly streetscapes, parking meter modernization, and shop-local incentives.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Expanding Public Speaking Time & Open Town Halls
keyPlatformPillars.details: Expand citizen public comment periods at council meetings and institute quarterly open town halls in each Clifton ZIP code so residents have direct access to their elected officials.

quotes: Small businesses and homeowners are the lifeblood of Clifton. We need a two-year tax freeze to let residents catch their breath, and a City Hall that listens to everyone.

councilCandidates.name: Norman A. Tahan
councilCandidates.role: Retired Clifton Deputy Fire Chief (35 Yrs), Former Councilman & BOE Member
councilCandidates.experience: 35 years of distinguished service in the Clifton Fire Department rising to Deputy Chief; served on Clifton City Council (1998–2002); served on Clifton BOE (2005–2008).
councilCandidates.tagline: Deep municipal operations knowledge, emergency service capital planning, stabilizing City Hall leadership, and cutting outside legal fees.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Restoring Stability, Trust & Experience to City Hall
keyPlatformPillars.details: Bring over 40 years of combined municipal public safety and elected governance experience to resolve administrative dysfunction, fill critical department head vacancies, and end costly internal lawsuits.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Long-Term Emergency Services Capital Planning
keyPlatformPillars.details: Develop a structured 10-year replacement cycle for fire trucks, ambulance rigs, and emergency equipment, eliminating emergency debt bonding and maintaining Clifton's Class 1 fire rating.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Cutting Wasteful Outside Litigation & Legal Fees
keyPlatformPillars.details: Reign in millions paid to outside law firms and specialized legal counsel by establishing stronger in-house legal oversight and preventing avoidable municipal litigation.

quotes: I spent 35 years protecting Clifton as a firefighter and Deputy Chief, and I know how every department in City Hall operates. We need steady, seasoned leadership to put Clifton back on track.
councilCandidates.civicBackground: Retired Deputy Fire Chief (Clifton Fire Dept, 35 yrs); Clifton City Council (1998–2002); Clifton BOE Trustee (2005–2008); FMBA Local 21.

outsideBusinesses: Retired Clifton Deputy Fire Chief (35 years in Clifton Fire Department)
Former Clifton City Councilman (1998–2002) & Former Clifton BOE Commissioner (2005–2008)
investigativeDossier.disclosuresAndFDS: Long public service record; state PFRS pension recipient. Clean corporate record.
investigativeDossier.cleanRecordVerification: Retired Deputy Fire Chief with documented public protests, Civil Service lawsuit, and social media controversies.

notableControversies.title: 2009 Deputy Fire Chief Promotion Protest & Internet Forum Remarks
notableControversies.details: When Tahan was slated for promotion from Captain to Deputy Fire Chief in May 2009, local residents and Jewish community organizations staged public protests and petitioned the Mayor and Council over derogatory, hostile online forum posts allegedly targeting the Jewish community and Clifton's Rosemawr neighborhood.
notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: Tahan defended his 25-year firefighting record, stated that he had previously apologized for the internet remarks, and noted he was cleared of formal departmental wrongdoing. City Council proceeded with the promotion, citing his decades of frontline service.

notableControversies.title: Civil Service Bypass Lawsuit (Tahan v. City of Clifton)
notableControversies.details: Tahan filed legal appeals and lawsuits against the City of Clifton after the city bypassed him (ranked #2 on the Civil Service Fire Chief eligibility list) to promote the #3 ranked candidate to Fire Chief. Tahan alleged procedural irregularity and denial of personnel records.
notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: The NJ Civil Service Commission rejected Tahan's appeal, and in August 2014, the New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division affirmed the ruling in favor of the City of Clifton, upholding municipal appointment discretion.

notableControversies.title: 2020 Social Media Post Backlash Regarding Civil Rights Protests
notableControversies.details: Tahan sparked severe public outrage and media coverage over an inflammatory social media comment regarding civil rights demonstrators ('If you are out at any of these 'protest' you are a scum bag and deserve to get shot'), drawing widespread community condemnation and calls for accountability.
notableControversies.resolutionOrOutcome: The comments were widely condemned by civic groups; Tahan subsequently retired from municipal service.

investigativeDossier.conflictOfInterestWatch: As a retired Deputy Fire Chief collecting a state PFRS pension, must recuse from any fire union grievance arbitrations or fire equipment vendor disputes involving former departmental associates.
